section.sectionSummaryBrief: Avraham attained the level of "all" through ten trials, teaching that divine service requires extraordinary effort, which brings the revelation of the hidden essential self.
section.t: Now, that which is related in the Oral Torah, that Avraham merited the aspect of "all" by standing in ten trials, is
(like all matters in Torah, from the word "hora'ah" [teaching]60)
a teaching that it must be
(similar to61)
the service of trials,
namely,
that the service must be with great effort,
effort that is not in the ordinary way,
similar to the service of trials.
And this is what is stated in the Zohar there on the verse62
"No eye has seen, etc., He will do for those who wait for Him,"
"What is 'for those who wait for Him'? ... Those who press into the word of wisdom, etc."
[And this matter in the Zohar comes in continuation of the explanation of "what is 'all',"
as brought in the maamar],
that through effort in Torah,
effort that is not in the ordinary way
[and as explained in the maamar, "those who press into the word of wisdom" is effort in the manner of Or Chozer (returning light)],
and from this it follows that also the fulfillment of the mitzvos will be with great effort
(in the manner of our sages' statement63
"Great is study that brings to action"),
including also the effort in spreading the wellsprings outward,
for in addition to the effort that must be in the study and understanding of the wellsprings
("pressing into the word of wisdom"),
there must be a special effort to spread the wellsprings outward,
to bring the wellsprings also to those who are outside,
"among the thorns,"
and through this "the Master, King Moshiach, will come"64,
for then there will be the revelation of the hidden essential self (Atzmus),
"No eye has seen,"
speedily in our days, literally.
